segments.arabic:
١٢٢٢١- أم كجّة الأنصاريّة «١»:
ذكر الواقديّ عن الكلبيّ في تفسيره، عن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس- أن أوس بن ثابت الأنصاري توفّي وترك ثلاث بنات وامرأة يقال لها أم كجّة، فقام رجلان من بني عمه يقال لهما: سويد، وعرفجة، فأخذا ماله ولم يعطيا امرأته ولا بناته شيئا، فجاءت أم كجّة إلى رسول اللَّه ﵌، فذكرت ذلك له، فنزلت آية المواريث، فساقه مطولا، وهذا ملخصه.
وتقدم بيان الاختلاف في اسمي ابني عمه في ترجمة أوس بن ثابت.
وأخرج أبو نعيم، وأبو موسى، من طريقه ثم من رواية سفيان، عن عبد اللَّه بن محمد بن عقيل، عن جابر، قال: جاءت أم كجة إلى النبي ﵌ فقالت: يا رسول اللَّه، إن لي ابنتين قد مات أبوهما وليس لهما شيء، فأنزل اللَّه ﷿:
لِلرِّجالِ نَصِيبٌ مِمَّا تَرَكَ الْوالِدانِ وَالْأَقْرَبُونَ وَلِلنِّساءِ نَصِيبٌ مِمَّا تَرَكَ الْوالِدانِ وَالْأَقْرَبُونَ [النساء: ٧] . ثم أنزل اللَّه ﷿: يُوصِيكُمُ اللَّهُ فِي أَوْلادِكُمْ لِلذَّكَرِ مِثْلُ حَظِّ الْأُنْثَيَيْنِ [النساء: ١١] .
قال أبو موسى: كذا قال: ليس لهما شيء، وأراد ليس يعطيان شيئا من ميراث أبيهما.
قلت: راوية عن سفيان هو إبراهيم بن هراسة ضعيف، وقد خالفه بشر بن المفضل، عن عبد اللَّه بن محمد، عن جابر،
أخرجه أبو داود من طريقه، قال: خرجنا مع رسول اللَّه ﵌ حتى جئنا امرأة من الأنصار في الأسواق، فجاءت المرأة بابنتين، فقالت: يا رسول اللَّه، هاتان بنتا ثابت بن قيس قتل معك يوم أحد، وقد أخذ عمهما مالهما كله، فلم يدع لهما مالا إلا أخذه، فما ترى يا رسول اللَّه؟ فو اللَّه لا ينكحان أبدا إلا ولهما مال، فقال: «يقضي اللَّه في ذلك» . قال: ونزلت: يُوصِيكُمُ اللَّهُ فِي أَوْلادِكُمْ ...
[النساء: ١١]، فقال رسول اللَّه ﵌: «ادع لي المرأة وصاحبها» . فقال لعمهما: «أعطهما الثّلثين، وأعط أمهما الثّمن، وما بقي فهو لك» .
(١) أسد الغابة ت (٧٥٧٦) .
segments.english:
12221—Umm Kajjah al-Ansariyyah (1):

Al-Waqidi mentioned, on the authority of al-Kalbi in the latter’s commentary, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, that Aws ibn Thabit al-Ansari died and left three daughters and a wife called Umm Kajjah. Then two of his paternal cousins, named Suwayd and Arfajah, came forward, took his property, and gave neither his wife nor his daughters anything. Umm Kajjah came to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and told him about this, whereupon the inheritance verse was revealed. He related the report at length; this is its summary.

The disagreement concerning the names of his two paternal cousins was explained previously in the entry on Aws ibn Thabit.

Abu Nu'aym transmitted it, and Abu Musa transmitted it through Abu Nu'aym’s route; it then comes through the narration of Sufyan, from Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Aqil, from Jabir, who said: Umm Kajjah came to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and said, “O Messenger of Allah, I have two daughters whose father has died, and they have nothing.” Allah, Mighty and Majestic, then revealed: “For men is a share of what parents and close relatives leave, and for women is a share of what parents and close relatives leave” [al-Nisa: 7]. Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: “Allah instructs you concerning your children: for the male is the equivalent of the share of two females” [al-Nisa: 11].

Abu Musa said: This is how he phrased it: “They have nothing,” but what he meant was that they were not being given anything from their father’s inheritance.

I say: The narrator from Sufyan is Ibrahim ibn Harasah, who is weak. Bishr ibn al-Mufaddal differed from him, narrating from Abd Allah ibn Muhammad, from Jabir. Abu Dawud transmitted it through his route. He said: We went out with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, until we came to a woman of the Ansar in the marketplaces. The woman came with two daughters and said, “O Messenger of Allah, these are the two daughters of Thabit ibn Qays, who was killed alongside you on the Day of Uhud. Their paternal uncle has taken all their property; he has not left them any property without taking it. What is your view, O Messenger of Allah? By Allah, they will never marry unless they possess property.” He said: “Allah will decide concerning that.” He said: Then the following was revealed: “Allah instructs you concerning your children ...” [al-Nisa: 11]. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, then said: “Call the woman and the man involved in her case for me.” He said to their paternal uncle: “Give the two of them two-thirds, give their mother one-eighth, and whatever remains is yours.”

(1) Usd al-Ghaba, entry (7576).

segments.arabic:
قال أبو داود: هذا خطأ، وإنما هما ابنتا سعد بن الرّبيع، وأما ثابت بن قيس فقتل باليمامة.
ثم
ساقه عن طريق ابن وهب: أخبرني داود بن قيس وغير من أهل العلم، عند عبد اللَّه بن محمد بن عقيل، عن جابر- أن امرأة سعد بن الربيع قالت: يا رسول اللَّه، إن سعدا هلك وترك ابنتين ... فساق نحوه. انتهى.
وأخرجه التّرمذيّ، والحاكم، من طريق عبيد اللَّه بن عمرو الرّقي، عن ابن عقيل، عن جابر، قال: جاءت امرأة سعد بن الرّبيع بابنتيها من سعد ... فذكر نحوه.
وهذا الّذي جزم به أبو داود من التخطئة هو الّذي تقتضيه قواعد أهل الحديث مع قيام الاحتمال، فقد اختلف في اسم الميت، فقيل ثابت بن قيس، وقيل أوس بن ثابت كما تقدّم، وقيل أوس بن مالك، واختلف في اسم هذا الّذي حاز المال على أقوال تقدّم بيانها في ترجمة أوس بن ثابت.
ومما لم يتقدّم من الاختلاف هناك أن الطّبري أخرج من طريق ابن جريج، عن عكرمة، قال: نزلت في أم كجّة، وبنت أم كجّة، وثعلبة، وأوس بن ثابت، وهم من الأنصار، أحدهما زوجها، والآخر عم ولدها، قالت: يا رسول اللَّه، مات زوجي وتركني، فلم نورث، فقال عمّ ولدها: لا تركب فرسا ولا تحمل كلّا، ولا تنكأ عدوا.
وأخرجه ابن أبي حاتم- من طريق محمد بن ثور، عن ابن جريج، قال: قال ابن عبّاس: نزلت في أم كلثوم، وبنت كجّة، وثعلبة بن أوس، وسويد، فذكر نحوه.
ومن طريق أسباط، عن السّديّ: كان أهل الجاهليّة لا يورثون الجواري ولا الضّعفاء من الذّكور، فمات عبد الرّحمن أخو حسّان الشّاعر، وترك امرأة يقال لها كجّة، وترك خمس حوار، فجاء العصبة فأخذوا ماله، فشكت أمّ كجّة ذلك للنبيّ ﵌. فأنزل اللَّه هذه الآية: فَإِنْ كُنَّ نِساءً فَوْقَ اثْنَتَيْنِ فَلَهُنَّ ثُلُثا ما تَرَكَ ... [النساء: ١١] الآية.
وأما المرأة فلم يختلف في أنها أم كجّة بضم الكاف وتشديد الجيم، إلا ما حكى أبو موسى عن المستغفريّ أنه قال فيها: أمّ كحلة، بسكون المهملة بعدها لام، وإلا ما تقدّم أنها بنت كجة في روايتي ابن جريج، فيحتمل أن تكون كنيتها وافقت اسم أبيها، وأما ابنتها فيستفاد من رواية ابن جريج أنها أم كلثوم.
segments.english:
Abu Dawud said: “This is an error. Rather, they were the two daughters of Sa'd ibn al-Rabi'. As for Thabit ibn Qays, he was killed at al-Yamama.”

Then he related it by way of Ibn Wahb: “Dawud ibn Qays and another of the scholars informed me, from 'Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn 'Aqil, from Jabir, that the wife of Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' said: ‘O Messenger of Allah, Sa'd died and left two daughters ...’” He then related a similar report. End of quotation.

al-Tirmidhi and al-Hakim also transmitted it by way of 'Ubayd Allah ibn 'Amr al-Raqqi, from Ibn 'Aqil, from Jabir, who said: “The wife of Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' came with her two daughters by Sa'd ...” He then mentioned a similar report.

This categorical judgment by Abu Dawud that the report was erroneous is what the principles of the hadith scholars require, although the possibility remains. There was disagreement regarding the deceased man's name: he was said to be Thabit ibn Qays; Aws ibn Thabit, as previously mentioned; or Aws ibn Malik. The name of the man who took possession of the estate was also disputed, several opinions having already been set out in the biography of Aws ibn Thabit.

Among the points of disagreement not previously mentioned there is the report that al-Tabari transmitted by way of Ibn Jurayj, from 'Ikrima, who said: “It was revealed concerning Umm Kujja and the daughter of Umm Kujja, and concerning Tha'laba and Aws ibn Thabit. They were among the Ansar; one of the two men was her husband and the other was her child's paternal uncle. She said: ‘O Messenger of Allah, my husband died and left me, but we were not made heirs.’ Her child's paternal uncle said: ‘She does not ride a horse, bear a burden, or wound an enemy.’”

Ibn Abi Hatim also transmitted it by way of Muhammad ibn Thawr, from Ibn Jurayj, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said, “It was revealed concerning Umm Kulthum and the daughter of Kujja, and concerning Tha'laba ibn Aws and Suwayd,” and he mentioned a similar report.

And by way of Asbat, from al-Suddi: “The people of the pre-Islamic period did not allow girls or weak males to inherit. 'Abd al-Rahman, the brother of Hassan the poet, died, leaving a wife called Kujja and five girls. The agnatic heirs came and took his property, so Umm Kujja complained about this to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. Allah then revealed this verse: ‘If they are women, more than two, then theirs shall be two-thirds of what he left ...’ [al-Nisa': 11], to the end of the verse.”

As for the woman, there was no disagreement that she was Umm Kujja—with a damma on the kaf and a doubled jim—except for what Abu Musa related from al-Mustaghfiri, who called her “Umm Kuhla,” with the undotted ha quiescent and followed by a lam; and except for the earlier statement in Ibn Jurayj's two reports that she was the daughter of Kujja. It is possible that her kunya matched her father's name. As for her daughter, Ibn Jurayj's report indicates that she was Umm Kulthum.
